title: Earldom of Ulster
capsule: The Earldom of Ulster was a major Anglo-Norman lordship in north-eastern Ireland, held by the de Burgh family from 1263. The period 1326–1333 represents the earldom's terminal phase: already weakened by Edward Bruce's invasion and siege of Carrickfergus (1315–1316), it collapsed in 1333 when William de Burgh, the 'Brown Earl,' was assassinated near Le Ford on the Bann by his own retainers. The murder ended effective de Burgh rule; the title passed through an heiress to the English Crown, but the territory contracted to coastal enclaves as Gaelic lords reclaimed the interior.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is moderately attested through charter evidence and annalistic records, but the precise boundaries of de Burgh control at any given year within 1326–1333 are uncertain given the disruption following the Bruce campaign.
